function.name: send_message
function.arguments: {"recipient_id": "C4", "purpose": "information", "message": "I'm building a phased migration plan for 120 workspaces with a March 31 deadline, 2 engineers, and migration capacity of 20/day. Two questions: (1) Is the 20/day capacity per engineer or total across both engineers? (2) What is the planned start date, since the packet only gives the deadline?"}

assistant_message.content: C4 did not answer either question. Their reply only mentions a preference about migrating the largest customer late. Since the plan works under either capacity reading, I'll build it on the conservative assumption and flag the open questions.

function.name: submit_answer
function.arguments: {"answer": {"baseline_summary": {"workspaces": 120, "deadline": "March 31", "migration_capacity_per_day": 20, "engineers": 2}, "recommendation": "Phased plan (conservative: 20 workspaces/day total across both engineers, i.e., 6 working days of migration capacity; if capacity is 20/day per engineer, total is 40/day and the schedule shortens to about 3 days). Phase 1 (pilot): migrate about 20 smaller/low-risk workspaces in the first working day to validate runbooks and rollback. Phase 2 (main wave): migrate the remaining bulk at up to 20/day across both engineers, with a daily checkpoint for failures and rollbacks; this takes about 5 more working days. Phase 3 (late wave): migrate the largest customer last, per the account owner's stated preference (a preference, not a contractual blackout), with a buffer day before March 31. Buffer: hold at least 1-2 days of slack before March 31 for rework. Open items: the planned start date is not stated, so the schedule must be checked against it; the capacity unit (total vs per engineer) is unconfirmed (C4 did not answer); and the workload assumes no other constraints.", "quality_notes": ["C4 did not answer the capacity-unit or start-date questions; their reply only addressed migration order.", "The 20/day capacity is interpreted conservatively as a team total; the per-engineer reading would make the plan finish sooner, so the plan holds under either reading.", "Start date is unknown, so feasibility against March 31 is assumed but not verified.", "Largest-customer-last ordering is a stated preference, not a hard constraint.", "No approvals were claimed or received."]}}
